reading:
Flight Console did not lose on its idea. It was the strongest newcomer of main round 11 (6.67, 7 promise votes). Feedback called it "fresh, period computing that keeps the CRT soul", and type called its flight-log chat and zero-padded readouts "the strongest console typography yet". Every lens named the readout strip (Today, Plans 05, To do 04, Late 02, Ideas 12) as the best glance in the round.

What the judges love:
- the readout strip;
- the flight-plan track, with arcs between numbered stops and hatched weekends;
- the crew board of lamps on To do;
- the T-minus setup countdown (feedback and style);
- the flight-log typesetting;
- a real tube warm-up and the green afterglow fading on cards (soul);
- one lamp language with words beside every lamp;
- Plex Sans / Plex Sans Condensed / Plex Mono with VT323 only on the glass.

What sank it, in order of how many lenses said it:
1. Tracked mono caps on the nav, buttons and every "ALL →" link. All eight lenses said it, in both rounds, and the nav's icons were swapped for square dots.
2. 23 targets under 44px on Home.
3. The Status annunciator repeats the three lists under it (feedback, soul, system, usability, skeptic, interaction). The crew board also repeats its list and needs decoding.
4. Costume that tells the family nothing: FIG. captions, "CONSOLE 09 | SYSTEMS" plates, HOLDS, T-3, Capcom.
5. A one-sided chat (system, interaction, skeptic).
6. Coming up is numbered from 2, because stop 1 is in the tube.
7. Amber means both "today" and "late" (skeptic).
8. Faint dashed violet arcs and violet dot-grid noise (skeptic, system, soul). The lessons now call violet off-period wherever it is more than a line.
9. Empty dotted tile columns, and full frames on every bay (style).
10. The kids' wishes sit above Coming up. Home is 2205px long.
11. The greeting's lit pool is weak (soul).

Its own crossover child, Slate Flight Console (r12-mut-3), fixed only the usability faults (sentence-case nav, 0 small targets, one job for amber, the rail as links). It beat the parent 6.96 to 6.02 in the same round. It stayed out of every top four because of the leftover costume, the 2100px Home and the Status caps tiles.

What would make it win:
- Keep every drawing the judges loved, but let each say one thing once: the rail says counts, the track says when, the rows say what, and the annunciator IS the Status rows.
- Make the rail the system's head element on every page. It carries the page's own figures, and each cell is a 44px link.
- Controls in sentence case, 44px keys, a filled steel "here", and today in steel so amber has one job.
- Relight exactly where the phosphor is: the mark and cursor, the lit key word, Send, the NOW needle and the Next stop, the lamps, the tubes, her screen, the greeting pool.
- Carry the console through Plans, To do, Settings and the form, not only Home.

Title: the lineage has no judged title yet, and the tour's lessons are empty. "What's on your mind?" is the carried words. The refinement proposes "What's the plan?" (lit: plan). The graft proposes "Tell Vera what's next." (lit: next), so the judges can compare a planner's question with an imperative that names her.

briefs.name: Flight Console, Go
briefs.hypothesis:
The structure was never the problem. Seven promise votes and 'best glance of the round' show that. The lineage's own child showed that fixing only the usability faults is worth about a point. This refinement does that and three things the child did not:
- It says each thing once. The rail gives counts. The track gives when, with its stops numbered to the rows. The rows give what. The annunciator becomes the Status rows' own designator column, so it is not a grid repeating them.
- It drops all the costume (FIG, CONSOLE nn, HOLDS, T-3) and keeps the countdown and flight-log ideas in plain words.
- It relights the phosphor exactly where it lives. The greeting pool, the NOW needle and Next stop, lit lamps in dark windows, full tubes.

The rail also becomes the one head element on every page, each page's own figures as 44px links. That turns a Home ornament into a system rule that holds on Plans, To do, Status and Settings. That should take it from 6.0-6.7 into the high 7s, alongside the leader.
briefs.brief: Start from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/t1-b/variants/r11-wild-3/ (sheet.css, templates/) and palettes/r11-wild-3.json. Keep its clean sheet, its three materials and its mood: grey console bays, ditto-violet flight-plan drawings, #6dff9c only as light. Copy /home/user/FamilyDB/src/familydb/web/templates/_ask.html into the variant's templates for the title. 1. TOKENS AND MATERIALS Bays tint a breath toward green-black (feedback): - --surface #111716 - --surface-2 #161d1b - --surface-3 #1c2422 - --card-edge #25302c - --line #212a27 - --line-2 #2f3a36 Ink calms to about 12.8:1: - --ink #d0d6cc - --heading #e8ebe4 - --ink-2 #aeb6ae - --dim #939c95 (keep every small text at 5:1 or more) Steel for "here" and "today": - --rev #6f8596 - --rev-cap #a9c4d8 - --rev-ink #070a09 (about 5.1:1) Ditto violet at lower chroma, lines only: - --ditto #a191bd - --ditto-2 #6f6384 Amber keeps ONE job, late and needs a look: words #f0b565, lamp var(--people). Bays (.bay, .console): - no side or bottom frame and no radius; - `border: 0; border-top: 2px solid var(--line-2)`, keeping the slate fill (grounded colour stays in a fill); - an inset 1px top highlight (kit E8); - the section's square lamp is hung at the rule's left end, level with the h2; - drop every screw. Delete the violet dot-grid backgrounds on .fig and .tile. .bay.slim becomes `grid-template-columns: 56px minmax(0,1fr)`: a plain gutter with its 26px pictogram in --ink-2 at the top, no fill. .fig keeps a plain --plot fill (#0d1110). Only the flight-plan figure gets a 16px steel graticule at 6%. 2. TYPE: one written scale - Page title 2.75rem Plex Sans Condensed 600, -0.01em. - Home's question 2.25rem Condensed 600. It is Home's largest words. - h2 1.375rem Condensed 600. - Row titles 1rem Plex Sans 600. - Body 1rem/1.55 Plex Sans 400. - Small 0.875rem. - Labels 0.8125rem Condensed 600 in sentence case, with no tracking. - Plex Mono 500 only for figures, dates and times: tabular-nums slashed-zero. - Tracked caps (0.06em, 0.75rem) survive only on chat callsigns and the annunciator state words. - text-wrap: balance on h1-h3; pretty on p and li. - Chat measure 62ch, ledes 58ch. 3. LAMPS: the lineage's own square console push-lights, one code The lamp() macro in _ui.html keeps its API: - on: a 10px lit square, #6dff9c with an inset white core and a halo of 0 0 4px brand/.8, 0 0 12px brand/.35. Only the one live thing breathes (3.2s): the chat model's row. - '' (open or waiting): an unlit square, #161b19 with a 1px #3a4541 rim. - off: a hollow round pewter ring, 10px, 1.5px #7d8781. - amber: late or needs a look. - red: stopped, only. Amber means "now" or "today" nowhere any more. Rewrite the lamp comments and task_legend to match. Delete every figcap() call and the .fig-n counter. Where lamps need a key (Status, To do's crew board) print one line in 0.8125rem Plex Sans, e.g. "Lit: working · Unlit: open · Ring: off · Amber: needs a look". 4. THE BAR In .places a, .tools > a and .menu > summary: - show the Lucide icon (remove `.places a .icon{display:none}`); - the word in Plex Sans 500 0.9375rem, sentence case, no letter-spacing; - keys 44px tall. Name Memory, Family, Status and Settings in words: remove the .tools .label clipping; below 1100px fall back to icons with labels. Drop the square dot lamp from every key but the current one. The current key ([aria-current=page], .menu.here > summary) is the latched steel key: - background var(--rev), ink var(--rev-ink), weight 600; - box-shadow: inset 0 2px 0 var(--rev-cap), 0 1px 0 #0008; - in its top-right corner, the lineage's lamp lit as a 6px #6dff9c LED with its halo. That is "a key's lamp lit where you are", now paired with a filled block so it survives the squint. Keep the FamilyDB mark and its blinking cursor at full light (E2). Phone tab bar: - words in sentence case under the icons; - "here" a tinted steel cell (#26313a) with a 2px var(--rev-cap) top cap and the LED. 5. THE READOUT RAIL: the system's global head element New macro `readout(label, figure, href=none, tone='')` in _ui.html; .rail restyled. - Each cell is an `` (min-height 56px, padding 10px 16px). - Label above: Condensed 600 0.8125rem, sentence case, --ink-2. - Figure below: Plex Mono 500 1.5rem, --heading, zero-padded to two digits (rail only). - Cells are split by 1px --line-2 rules on a --surface-2 strip with an E8 top highlight. - Hover: a 12% steel wash and the figure brightening, fading over var(--afterglow). - Visible focus ring, offset inside the cell. - tone='late' and tone='look': amber figure with an amber lamp before the label, shown only when above 0. - The Today cell reads "Tue 29 Sep" in Plex Mono 1.25rem in steel ink #a9c4d8. Never amber. It links to the month. Every inner page's head is: title and lede on the left, the page's one primary on the title's baseline at the right, then its rail. The rail carries that page's own figures, computed in its template from the context it already has (base.html has no counts): - Home: Today | Plans 05 (/plans) | To do 04 (/tasks) | Late 02 (/tasks) | Ideas 12 (/ideas) | Setup 03 (/setup). HOLDS is renamed. - Ideas: Ideas 12 | On the radar 10 | Nearest 18 min | Restaurants 2 (/restaurants). - Plans month: Today | This month 3 | Next: Pho Oregon, today. - To do: Open 4 | Late 2 | Due this week 1 | No date 1. - Status: Working 6 | Off 7 | Needs a look 0 | Spent today $0.00. These link to #models, #keys, #services and #spend, and land with the kit's E10 flash. - Settings: Parts 9 | Needs a look 1 | Today $0.00 of $2.00. Delete the page_head plate (.plate, .plate-row lens, the --pos/--console custom properties, "CONSOLE 09 | SYSTEMS"). Keep crumbs as underlined sentence-case links. 6. LIGHT (only where the phosphor is) - E1: the key word at 36px. - E2: the mark and cursor. - E3: ring and pool on the one primary per view. - E4: box glow, and Home's resting halo 0 0 38px -20px brand/.6 with its border at 38% brand. - E5: focus. - E6: top haze. - E7 relit: in .welcome-words, radial-gradient(70% 90% at 0% 100%, rgb(109 255 156/.14), transparent 62%) under the ask box, with the 1-in-4 scanlines masked to it (the soul lens asked for the pool back). - E9: the card afterglow the judges saw, extended to rows as a 12% steel wash plus a 2px #86d9a6 inset left edge, on at .12s, fading over 1.2s, also on :focus-within. - E10. - E12-E17 on every tube at full strength: VT323 with three halos and 0.35px blur, scanlines, sheen, vignette, radar sweep afterglow, glowing blips. - E16 warm-up on Next up. - E19 her screen. - E20 lit lamps. Monitor cases get thinner: - 6px sides and top, an 18px chin with a 1px groove and the power LED; - border-radius 14px, hairline lip inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255/.08); - no screws; - the 80px spill kept. 7. HOME (1280 target: 1750px or less, 0 targets under 44px) a) .welcome.console - The rail runs across its top. - Left: Next up's monitor, sized to its content (align-self:start, no dead glass). - Right: her screen with "Vera", then the ask box. Its h1 label is "What’s the plan?" (curly apostrophe), with textarea rows=3. - The From row: From, Send where I am, the mic, and Send (sentence case, E3). - Ways to start: three sentence-case keys, 44px, 8px gap. - If her last line exists, show it as one flight-log entry (VERA callsign in lit #86d9a6 plus a mono stamp, words below), then "Continue with Vera". b) Setup, when there is any: .bay.slim.setup with a 2px #7a5f33 amber top rule. - The 56px gutter stacks amber RINGS, one per step left (system asked for rings), over a dark square lamp labelled "Ready" (GO renamed). - The head reads "Finish setting up", then an amber lamp and "3 to go" in Plex Mono amber, with "All the setup steps" at the right. - Steps are ol.holds rows, 44px min, numbered 1, 2, 3 in Plex Mono --ink-2 (not T-3), each an underlined link. c) The flight plan and Coming up (.bay.bay-wide.coming#coming). The kids' wishes no longer come before it. The figure is 104px tall, with no caption: - The axis carries day ticks and week labels "Now, 1 wk, 2 wk, 3 wk, 4 wk" in Plex Mono 11px --ink-2. No uppercase. - Weekends are hatched in steel (#2f3a36 at 60%). - The NOW needle is lit #6dff9c 1.5px with the E20 halo and a lit 4px foot. - Next up's stop is a lit square lamp with "Next" above it in #86d9a6 11px, matching the tube. - Every later stop is a 20px ring (1.5px --ditto), numbered 1..n in --ink Plex Mono 600 11px. The numbers are the rows' numbers. - Arcs are SOLID 1.5px --ditto (not dashed). Height follows the gap, capped at 44px. Each apex carries the leg's length ("3 days", Plex Mono 11px --ink-2 on a --plot patch), so an arc says something the rows do not (skeptic: faint arcs "tell little"). - Drop the day numbers under the stops (the rows carry dates). The head reads "Coming up" + "4 after Next up" (Plex Mono 0.875rem --ink-2) + "All plans →" at the right (underlined, sentence case). The source note stays muted. ol.agenda becomes one-line hop rows (48px, 1px --line dividers), with grid 2rem 7.5rem minmax(0,1fr) 4rem 6.5rem: - the numbered ring, the same drawing as its stop; - "Thu 1 Oct" in Plex Mono; - the title link in 600, with its location muted after a middle dot; - a dotted leader to the time "10:00" in Mono (leader only where a fact follows, capped at 46rem); - the relative "in 2 days" in --ink-2, right-aligned. A plan today shows "today" in the steel reverse key. d) .duo desk The LEFT column is the To do bay: - The head reads "To do" + "4 open · 2 late" (2 late amber, linking to /tasks) + "All 4 things to do →". - The crew board becomes a compact strip under the head, with no figure column. A row per person: the name in Plex Sans 600 0.875rem (sentence case), their square lamps, then words at the right: "1 late, 1 open". Board and list now say different things. - Checklist rows: the 44px tick key (20px box drawn in it), the title in 600, then a meta line: who · due words. Late shows an amber lamp before "was due 2 days ago" in amber. The RIGHT column: - Lately added: 2x2 punched cards with the cut corner. Each has a kind lamp lens, the kind word in sentence case at 0.8125rem, the title, and "for Maya, Theo"; E9 edge afterglow. Then the "Something to eat" row. The section links read "Add an idea" and "All 12 ideas", underlined. - Under it, the kids' wishes: a slim bay with 56px gutter, kids as rows (name link, "0 open" in Mono, top wishes). Balance the two columns' feet. e) Phone - The rail becomes a 3x2 grid, Today across the top. - Tube, then box. The question is 2rem on one line. - Full-width starters. - Under 40rem the track keeps its needle, stops and rings but drops the leg labels, and the hop rows stack time and relative under the title. 8. CHAT (Vera) - Page head with her screen tile. No rail. - The thread sits on a --surface tray. The loop tile (her screen wired to each speaker's ring) stays in a 56px gutter with no dot grid. - A TWO-SIDED flight log. Vera (.said-bot) is on the left: a 28px glyph screen, the callsign "VERA" (Condensed 600 0.75rem 0.06em caps, lit #86d9a6) and the mono stamp "27 Sep, 19:48" (--ink-2) on the entry's top line, words below on green-black glass #0e1612 with a 1px brand-30% edge and her 9% pool from the top-left. - The family (.said-them) is right-aligned: a 28px steel initial key at the right, callsign and stamp in the plate's top line, words on slate #1b2327 with a 1px #33404a edge and a 3px #a9c4d8 inset bar on the edge facing the speaker. Max 62ch. The dashed rules go. - Composer at the foot, with Send in sentence case. 9. IDEAS - The head's primary is "Add an idea" (sentence case, E3), then the rail. - The radar monitor (E12-E17) sits left, with `white-space:nowrap` only on the [18 MIN NW] .dist span. - Filters sit right: - All ideas / Restaurants as latched steel keys with the LED; - Search, Kind, Status, For; - a secondary "Filter" key; - "Save a thought for later" as a full-width disclosure row. - No caption. "12 ideas" moves into the rail. - Punched cards stay 3-up: kind word in sentence case, #N in Mono, E9 afterglow. 10. PLANS (month) - List / Month as latched keys with the LED, then the rail. - The flight plan over the month uses Home's exact drawing language: numbered violet rings for this month's plans, the lit NOW needle, steel-hatched weekends, day numbers in Plex Mono 11px. Drop the lamp row under the axis and the caption. - Month grid: - day heads in sentence case ("Mon"); - weekend columns in --surface-2; - past days dimmed to --bg with --ink-2 numerals; - TODAY's numeral in the steel reverse key, not amber; - each plan in a cell shows its numbered ring and title link. - Earlier / Later are sentence-case 44px keys. The month name is 1.75rem Condensed. 11. TO DO - Head and rail. - The top bay: crew board on the left (16rem, --surface-2, rows with words, one-line legend); controls on the right. The Show select is replaced by latched keys for its statuses (one control per filter). Search and a Filter key follow. "Add something to do" is a full-width disclosure row. - The list is ONE bay of one-line checklist rows, not 3-up cards. Grid 44px 3rem minmax(0,1fr) 7rem 12rem 6rem: - the tick key; - #id in Mono --ink-2; - the title in 600, notes muted below; - who; - due words: "Was due 2 days ago" in amber with an amber lamp, or "Due in 2 days" in --ink-2, with "Sun 27 Sep, 19:56" in small Mono beneath; - an "Edit" key (44px, pencil icon) whose details open the existing form full-width under the row. - Late rows carry a 3px amber inset bar at the left. - Keep the template's session-clock lateness for the harness. Note in the design that views.task_row needs a `late` flag. 12. STATUS: the annunciator IS the rows - Head and rail. The attention panel comes first when present, with an amber top rule. - One bay of three banks in columns: Who answers, Keys, Connected to. Each h2 has its icon and a tally in Mono, e.g. "3 of 4". - Each row = an annunciator window (7rem x 44px min, recessed: #0a0f0d with inset 0 1px 3px #000a, 2px radius), then the name (Plex Sans 600, sentence case), the detail muted, and any action ("Use X instead") as a secondary key. - The window holds the square lamp and a state word in 0.75rem Condensed 600 caps, following the dark cockpit: - WORKING: dark glass with the lamp lit and the word in #86d9a6 with a slight text-shadow. No green fill. - OFF: the pewter ring, the word in --ink-2. - NEEDS A LOOK: a 2px amber top edge, 8% amber wash, amber lamp and word. - STOPPED: a red lamp and word. - Seen squinting, the windows read as the annunciator column. - Delete the separate .annunciator grid and its caption. One-line lamp legend at the bay's foot. - The spend bay (#spend) keeps its readout tube (E12-E17; --phosphor amber near and red past the limit), with the words beside it. 13. SETTINGS The index: head and rail, then the 3x3 cards, each a whole-card link: - the 56px gutter holds the pictogram (24px, --ink-2) with the part's lamp under it: lit square = set up, amber = needs a look, ring = off or not set; - title 1.0625rem 600, summary lines muted; - "Needs a look" as amber words after its lamp, not a caps chip; - the E9 edge afterglow. Section pages (General): - The settings nav is a column of 44px keys (icon + word), "here" as the steel latched key with the LED. No caption. - Groups are bays with top rules. - Field labels in sentence case, Plex Sans 600 0.875rem. Help in --ink-2 0.875rem at 60ch. - The sticky save bar holds "Save" as the primary. 14. THE FORM (new idea) - Crumbs "Ideas /", title "New idea". - Remove the punched-card figure column: one bay, fields in a 2-column grid. - Labels in sentence case. The optional ones say "optional" in --ink-2, as the task form does. - "Add it" primary and "Cancel" secondary, in sentence case. 15. SIGN IN AND 404 - Sign in keeps the face monitor with E22 and E16 and "READY." with its cursor. Drop the "CONSOLE 00 | GROUND" plate. Label "Family password"; "Sign in" in sentence case. - 404 keeps the radar with E18 flicker. 16. WISHES, FAMILY, MEMORY They inherit the bays' top rules, the sentence-case keys, the lamp code and the rail where they have counts (Wishes: Open 0 · Lists 2). Keep the reduced-motion, more-contrast and forced-colours blocks. In forced colours, lamps and windows are outlined and a lit lamp is CanvasText. Keep every csrf and once token and every sprite icon. No inline style. Words changed, to say in the notes: - the title; - Holds becomes Setup, and "3 to go" replaces T-3; - Go becomes Ready; - "4 after Next up"; - the rail labels.
briefs.borrows:
The judges' own fixes, most-cited first:

1. Sentence-case nav, buttons and see-more links at text size, with the icons back and the links underlined. All 8 lenses in r11 and r12: feedback, soul, style, system, interaction, type, usability, skeptic.

2. The readout rail as 44px links: Late to To do, Plans to Plans, Setup to setup. Interaction, usability, system and skeptic in r11; interaction, usability and skeptic on the child in r12. It also becomes a global element on every page (style: "carry a slim version on every page"; system: "make it the system's global element"), with Plex Mono figures and sentence-case labels.

3. The annunciator no longer repeats the Status lists. It becomes their designator column: dark-cockpit windows in sentence-case rows with state words. Feedback, soul, system, usability and skeptic in r11; interaction and usability in r12.

4. 0 targets under 44px. Interaction, system and usability.

5. Drop FIG captions, CONSOLE nn plates, HOLDS and T-3; rename to Setup and "3 to go". Feedback, usability, skeptic and type in r12, interaction in r12. The countdown's amber lamps become rings (system).

6. A two-sided chat that keeps the flight-log typesetting (system, interaction, skeptic; type keeps the log).

7. Stops numbered to match the rows, with Next up as the lit "Next" stop and the head "4 after Next up" (system, usability, interaction; lessons r13).

8. Today in steel reverse so amber has one job (skeptic, lessons r8-r10).

9. Violet only as solid legible lines, at lower chroma, with no dot grids and never as text. Feedback, soul, skeptic ("read at 100%"), system ("dot-grid noise").

10. Bays with one top rule, no screws, tinted a breath toward green-black, and empty tile columns collapsed to a 56px gutter (style, feedback).

11. Coming up before the kids' wishes; wishes beside To do in the desk; Home cut toward 1700px (interaction, usability).

12. The greeting pool relit under the question. The tube warm-up and the afterglow kept (soul).

13. Body in Plex Sans with Condensed kept for heads, plus text-wrap to end the widows (type).

14. The crew board says per-person words, so it no longer repeats the list (usability).

15. One-line To do rows instead of 3-up cards (system, r12).

Small borrowings, each answering a fault:
- The lineage's own child, Slate Flight Console: the rail-as-links markup, in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r12/variants/r12-mut-3/templates/home.html lines 68-75 and sheet.css .rail and .readout-cell (lines 569-587); and its chat split rules, sheet.css .thread > li.said-them and .said-bot (891-902).
- The steel values for "here" from L186 (r10-mut-5, its palette css), darkened per lessons r11.
- Its own L104 card afterglow, extended to rows per the lessons' fix.
- The phosphor kit E1-E22 for the light.
briefs.title: What’s the *plan*? It is a question the family already asks each other ("so what's the plan for Saturday?"). It names FamilyDB's job as their planner: weekends and outings, plans on the calendar, and the things to do that go with them. It invites telling Vera, because a plan can be an idea to keep, a reminder or a date. It fits the lineage exactly, since the page under it is the family's flight plan. It is 16 characters, so it fits one line on a phone at 2rem. The lit word is "plan", the one the whole console is about.

briefs.name: Lamps and Ladders
briefs.hypothesis:
The console already had the right skeleton. What it lacked was instruments that carry real light. Four features rebuilt as a 1969 console's hardware do that:
- A glowing T-minus lamp ladder on every hop (L043, a gem).
- Jewelled glass pilot lamps (L097, a gem).
- One four-shape lamp code with a key (L260).
- A phosphor moving-coil panel meter on Status (L215).

These put the original page's glowing dots on the black back as data, each with a job. The soul and feedback lenses reward exactly that, and the lessons' 'light as data' asks for it. The lamp code also fixes amber's two jobs and the red rings that read as alarms. The lineage's usability fixes come with it: sentence-case 44px keys, the rail as links, a two-sided log, no costume. So it should keep Flight Console's glance and gain a lit instrument on Home, To do, Plans and Status, reading as a finished console rather than a costume.
briefs.title: Tell Vera what’s *next*. (rendered as "Tell {{ assistant }} what’s next.", her name from personas.) It is an invitation in the family's voice. It names how FamilyDB works (you tell her) and what it is for: the next weekend, the next plan on the calendar, the next thing to do or be reminded of. "Next" is the console's own live word: the Next up screen, the next hop on the flight plan and the ladders counting down to it. So the lit word ties the question to the lit instruments below. At 22 characters it fits one line on a phone at 2rem. It differs from the refinement's question, so the judges can compare a question with an imperative that names her.
